translation_notes: Genuine typed-literal case (one of the stratum's true 36/85, not the measurement artefact of Warning 1): only lowerBound carries datatype=XSD.nonNegativeInteger. Verified by direct execution (both bare and inside an island) that lower_bound is always a str (regex capture group in the real cardinalities.py), so Literal(v, datatype=XSD.nonNegativeInteger) and {v}^^xsd:nonNegativeInteger are the exact same term -- Trap 1 (2 bis) does not bite because the value is already a string.
cardinalityValue and upperBound are Literal(str) with no datatype= (Warning 1): kept as bare {expr} interpolation, no ^^ added.
RDF.type rewritten as Turtle's 'a' shorthand (migrate-from-rdflib.md's own canonical mapping) rather than a declared @prefix rdf:, since nothing else in the region needs the rdf: namespace.
@graph ontouml_graph designates the function's own graph parameter (matches migrate-from-rdflib.md: g.add(...) -> +{ } with @graph g).

The three original .add() calls are not a contiguous same-subject run (subjects alternate cardinality-individual / property-individual / cardinality-individual), so kept as three separate +{ } islands; only the trailing lowerBound/upperBound pair, which IS contiguous and same-subject, is merged into one +{ s p1 o1 ; p2 o2 } run.

Executability: the real source uses relative imports (from ..modules import ...) two packages up, which cannot resolve under rdfeval.harness's exec()-based execution (no __package__ set). Rewritten in original.py and translated.ldpy alike to absolute imports against a local modules/ context shim: modules/arguments.py (ARGUMENTS defaults matching the project's own library/test-mode initialisation), modules/utils_graph.py (ontouml_ref + METADATA["conformsTo"], copied verbatim), modules/cardinalities.py (resolve_cardinality and its helpers, copied verbatim in full), and modules/decode_obj_property_predecl.py (determine_cardinality_bounds, copied verbatim from the same source file's lines 194-211, just above this region). No logic invented; all shim content is copied from OntoUML/ontouml-json2graph@982f12b9c4.

Driver exercises three cases: a normal numeric range (typed lowerBound), a '*' upper bound (lower_bound='0' still typed, upper_bound='*' stays plain), and an unparsable/unrepairable cardinality under the 'preserve' policy (bounds stay None on both sides, verifying the guarded lowerBound/upperBound block is skipped identically). Sabotage-tested: dropping ^^xsd:nonNegativeInteger from the lowerBound triple makes rdfeval check fail (graphs not isomorphic), confirming the pilot actually discriminates this construction.
